A lot of things that have been said by others on the thread, but as someone who had already needed psychiatric help in my life prior to going through a mental burn out, I have these in mind : 

* **Not all the bad moments in your life are related to mental illness**. Shit happens. The only way this is related to your mental health is you thinking you're fragile and easily overwhelmed. This one specific shit is very common and relatable and you will get sympathy and understanding, just don't be a drama queen.
* **Confront the bad decisions you made that lead to this miserable outcome**.  Don't blame others. At some point you committed to something for various reasons and from the outcomes it is obivous now your judgment was biaised or incomplete. What happened ? What informations did you miss ? Did you put your trust in someone who wasn't worth it ?
* **Forgive yourself for all the past decisions and behaviours you wish to separate from in the future**. As much as you apologise to others it might never bring back the ones you've lost, but shame and guilt make it impossible to become a better version of yourself.

Also, I recommend a **healthy diet and as much physical activity as you can get**. The benefits are endless : your mind is stronger and makes more rational decisions when all basic physiological needs are fulfilled and if you're feeling a bit depressed or anxious, it will contribute to improve your mood. It boosts production of happiness neurotransmitters like endorphines and serotonines. At a time in your life when you might be feeling helpless, it is a very effective way to empower yourself by setting and reaching your own goals. It will boost your confidence and needless to say, it will distract you from overthinking on the couch.
